title: An = in the folder name wipes the setting
summary: Drop the hand written key=value file and let QSettings do it. Pass value a default, and set the organization and application names before the first QSettings.

turns.user: I write settings to ~/.notepad.conf by hand and if the folder name has an = in it, lastDir is gone next launch. doesnt Qt have something for this already

assistant.body: Great catch! The culprit is split('='). Only lines that split into exactly two parts were read, so a value containing = came out as three parts and the whole line was dropped. Qt has QSettings for this, so the hand written file goes away. Qt picks the format and the location for each OS. The second argument to value is the default for a key that is not there yet. A QSettings built with no arguments finds its storage from the organization and application names, so main sets them first. Note: if either is missing, nothing is read or written at all, and status() reports AccessError.

turns.user: works. while youre at it remember the window size and position too. oh and whether it was maximized

assistant.body: Sure thing. saveGeometry packs the size, the position and the maximized state into one QByteArray. Save it on close and hand it back to restoreGeometry at startup. On the very first launch nothing has been saved, so value returns an empty QByteArray, restoreGeometry just returns false, and the window opens at its default size.
